claim: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) accounts for approximately 10–20% of all breast cancers.
source: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), defined as estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) negative, accounts for approximately 10–20% of all breast cancers (Costa et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Costa et al., 2017

claim: TNBC is characterized by higher tumor mutation burden than other breast cancer subtypes.
source: Characterized by higher tumor mutation burden and more intensive tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes infiltration in tumor microenvironment (TME) (Loi et al., 2019), TNBC is more sensitive to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) than any other subtypes (Keenan and Tolaney, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Loi et al., 2019

claim: TNBC is characterized by more intensive tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes infiltration in tumor microenvironment.
source: Characterized by higher tumor mutation burden and more intensive tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes infiltration in tumor microenvironment (TME) (Loi et al., 2019), TNBC is more sensitive to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) than any other subtypes (Keenan and Tolaney, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Loi et al., 2019

claim: TNBC is more sensitive to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) than any other breast cancer subtypes.
source: Characterized by higher tumor mutation burden and more intensive tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes infiltration in tumor microenvironment (TME) (Loi et al., 2019), TNBC is more sensitive to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) than any other subtypes (Keenan and Tolaney, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Keenan and Tolaney, 2020

claim: The combination with pembrolizumab and standard chemotherapy is recommended for TNBC patients with stages II–III according to NCCN guidelines.
source: Nowadays, the combination with pembrolizumab (a PD-1 blockade) and standard chemotherapy is recommended for TNBC patients with stages II–III according to National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guidelines (Gradishar et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to NCCN guidelines (Gradishar et al., 2022)

claim: Around 40% of TNBC patients cannot achieve a pathological complete response with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy.
source: However, there is still around 40% of TNBC patients cannot achieve a pathological complete response (pCR) according to KEYNOTE-522 (Schmid et al., 2020) and IMpassion031 (Mittendorf et al., 2020) trials, which call for more promising strategies.
evidence: Supported by citations to KEYNOTE-522 and IMpassion031 trials

claim: Approximately half of cancer patients may receive radiotherapy during the entire treatment period.
source: Radiotherapy (RT) is the most critical locoregional treatment in solid malignancies and approximately half of patients may receive radiotherapy during the entire treatment period (Atun et al., 2015; Citrin, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Atun et al., 2015 and Citrin, 2017

claim: SBRT can shorten treatment time and reduce exposure to the surrounding tissues.
source: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT), a novel technique with higher doses of radiation delivery to the tumor lesion in a smaller number of fractions, can shorten treatment time and reduce exposure to the surrounding tissues (Chen et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2020

claim: SBRT has already been widely applied to advanced breast cancer as salvage treatment targeting osseous and brain metastasis or other oligometastatic sites.
source: SBRT has already been widely applied to advanced breast cancer as salvage treatment targeting to osseous and brain metastasis or other oligometastatic sites (Nicosia et al., 2022; Viani et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nicosia et al., 2022 and Viani et al., 2021

claim: Preoperative SBRT may be advantageous for downstaging the tumor to enable breast conservation and improving pCR rate.
source: Preoperative SBRT may be advantageous for downstaging the tumor to enable breast conservation and improving pCR rate (Piras et al., 2023) and multiple trials investigating neoadjuvant SBRT in various malignancies (Holyoake et al., 2021; Kishi et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2022; Novikov et al., 2021) are currently ongoing.
evidence: Supported by citation to Piras et al., 2023

claim: Multiple trials investigating neoadjuvant SBRT in various malignancies are currently ongoing.
source: Preoperative SBRT may be advantageous for downstaging the tumor to enable breast conservation and improving pCR rate (Piras et al., 2023) and multiple trials investigating neoadjuvant SBRT in various malignancies (Holyoake et al., 2021; Kishi et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2022; Novikov et al., 2021) are currently ongoing.
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple ongoing trials

claim: SBRT has immunomodulatory properties by inducing cancer cell death to boost neoantigen-specific memory immune response.
source: In addition, preclinical evidence suggested that SBRT has immunomodulatory properties by inducing cancer cells death to boost neoantigen-specific memory immune response and upregulate the expression of PD-L1 on tumor cells (Deng et al., 2014; Han et al., 2022; Park et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to preclinical studies (Deng et al., 2014; Han et al., 2022; Park et al., 2015)

claim: SBRT upregulates the expression of PD-L1 on tumor cells.
source: In addition, preclinical evidence suggested that SBRT has immunomodulatory properties by inducing cancer cells death to boost neoantigen-specific memory immune response and upregulate the expression of PD-L1 on tumor cells (Deng et al., 2014; Han et al., 2022; Park et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to preclinical studies (Deng et al., 2014; Han et al., 2022; Park et al., 2015)

claim: Patients aged between 18 and 75 years with histologically confirmed invasive TNBC and pathological tumor size ≥2.0 cm in MRI assessment were eligible for enrollment.

evidence: Describes the inclusion criteria for the study

claim: All patients intravenously received 8 cycles of adebrelimab (20 mg/kg every 3 weeks).

claim: SBRT (24 Gy/3 f) targeted to breast lesion was started at the second cycle every other day.
